newsitem.title: USA: Government rejects Staples-Office Depot merger.
newsitem.headline: Government rejects Staples-Office Depot merger.

text.p: A government agency Monday rejected the proposed $4 billion merger of Staples Inc. and Office Depot Inc. and prepared to try to block the deal in federal court this week.

The Federal Trade Commission voted 4 to 1 to seek an injunction by a March 13 deadline. If a judge grants the injunction, the FTC would then plan for an administrative trial, a process that would take months or even years.
"Staples and Office Depot are the two largest operators of office supply superstores in the country," said William Baer, director of the FTC's bureau of competition.
"The fact is that in those communities where Staples faces competition from Office Depot, prices are significantly lower than where it does not."
He said if the merger were allowed to proceed, "competition will be reduced or eliminated and consumers will pay higher prices."

The FTC said the companies compete in about 40 cities and that if they merged to form a chain of more than 1,000 stores, competition would be reduced in California, Florida, Illinois, Kentucky, Maryland, Michigan, New Jersey, New York, North and South Carolina, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, Washington, Indiana, Utah and in Washington D.C.
